text:
maria: hey team — running into a packaging/install problem in a customer's CI. they use poetry and `poetry install` fails when resolving/redownloading `redwood-sdk` because a wheel build step errors out.

maria: error snippet:
```
Building wheel for redwood-sdk (pyproject.toml) ... error
ERROR: Failed building wheel for redwood-sdk
  × Building wheel for redwood-sdk (pyproject.toml) did not run successfully.
  │ exit code: 1
  ╰─> See above for output.
...
RuntimeError: 'manylinux_2_17_x86_64' wheel is not supported on this platform
```

maria: they repro locally w/ ubuntu:22.04 and python 3.10. pip is 22.3 inside the poetry venv.

sam: hmm, that sounds like a wheel tag incompatibility. older pip/packaging don't understand some newer manylinux tags. first try: upgrade pip to latest (>=23.1) inside the venv.

sam: also check if poetry is building from source because wheel for that platform isn't available on PyPI. `pip download --no-binary :all: redwood-sdk` to force-build and see details.

jamie: another angle: we should publish manylinux2014/manylinux_2_28 wheels for x86_64 and aarch64. we currently only ship a source wheel + a single manylinux build that may be tagged incorrectly. using cibuildwheel would help produce correct tags.

patrick: fwiw there's also an async/typing packaging issue I hit earlier: mypy complains because there are no PEP 561 stubs/py.typed in the wheel. that makes consumers who compile with strict typing break.

patrick: example: `from redwood import AsyncClient` works at runtime but mypy says "module has no attribute 'AsyncClient'" because the package isn't typed. shipping `py.typed` and proper type hints in the package (or a bundled .pyi) would fix it.

maria: also saw dependency pin conflicts in the customer's poetry.lock — protobuf got pinned to 4.23.x by another dep and redwood-sdk had `<4.23` which made poetry fail to resolve.

sam: oh that explains it. poetry's resolver will try to build from sdist if binary wheel for the platform isn't matched AND dependency constraints clash. two fixes: relax the protobuf spec to a compatible range, or publish wheels for the common protobuf versions.

jamie: agreed. proposed checklist for a patch release:
- relax protobuf version spec to `>=4.21,<5` or similar
- make async deps optional extras (`redwood-sdk[async]`) and ensure extras are documented in quickstart
- include `py.typed` and add PEP561 metadata
- publish manylinux2014/x86_64 + aarch64 wheels via cibuildwheel
- update docs: poetry install note + `poetry add redwood-sdk --extras \"async\"`

patrick: I'll open a PR for the packaging changes (dependency bounds + py.typed). I'll also add a tiny typing stub for AsyncClient while we migrate the runtime types.

maria: awesome. for the immediate workaround I told the customer to `pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel` inside their CI before `poetry install` and that unblocked them.

deploy-bot: release published: redwood-sdk 0.8.4 -> PyPI (https://pypi.org/project/redwood-sdk/0.8.4) :rocket:

patrick: PR is up: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/542 — relax protobuf, add py.typed, add packaging CI for manylinux. needs review.

jamie: i'll review later today. we should also add a short note in onboarding quickstart about `poetry` quirks and recommended `pip` versions.

maria: thanks all — passing back to customer. closing once PR merges. :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks :tada:
